questions.question: OP-01/O65 (async methods): the async stream's tell/readable/seekable/seek/truncate/write were answered 'All awaited' twice on 2026-10-31 (log 07bd66b7, lost in a worker restart), then 'I/O awaited, rest plain' on 2026-11-01 (fa0b580f), which D101 adopts. Which stands?

options.label: D101 stands (Recommended)
options.description: Methods making a request (read, read1, readinto, readline, close) are coroutines; tell, readable, seekable, seek, truncate, write plain. The latest answer, its reason that awaiting local state gains nothing. Source: asyncio.StreamReader.at_eof; trio wrap_file and anyio AsyncFile keep readable/seekable plain (from recall, not run).

options.label: All awaited
options.description: Every method a coroutine, D101 withdrawn and D69's plain-methods sentence withdrawn, as the two earlier answers had it. One rule for callers (await everything), as aiofiles does; costs an await on pure local state.

options.label: trio/anyio split
options.description: tell, seek, truncate coroutines too; readable, seekable plain. Matches trio/anyio (from recall, not run), but tell makes no request here, so the split has no reason of its own in OP-01.

questions.question: OP-01/O65 (shared blocks): what a shared item blocks was answered 'Blocks sentence each' (07bd66b7, 08:17Z: a shared item blocks its landing only, OP-01's spec stating the decision for OP-01), then 'Per item, as listed' (cbcf16f7, 10:21Z), which D108 adopts (shared items hold back OP-01's own clauses until landed). Which stands?

options.label: D108 stands (Recommended)
options.description: No clause is written before its home is known, so there is one copy. Costs no wait beyond OP-01's own flow, which shared.md names as the filler of Handle, Lifetime, State, the error layer's home and the timeout bound (only O5 also waits on OP-21's flow).

options.label: Landing only
options.description: OP-01's spec states each shared decision for OP-01 now; the shared item blocks only its own landing. Spec can be written sooner, but the landing flow must then move or cite the clause, two copies until it does. D108 and D111 withdrawn.

questions.question: OP-01/O65 (provenance): the Session names neither earlier answer nor log fa0b580f; O52's and O58's read1 questions were also answered twice, the options differing in form only. Amend the Session?

options.label: Session line (Recommended)
options.description: Session gains a line naming log 07bd66b7's earlier answers (O58 async twice, O64, O51's 'Reads only'), log fa0b580f, and which answer stands per this reopen; the read1 double answers differ in form only, so D96 and D100 stand.

options.label: As is
options.description: Leave the Session; O65 and this reopen's decisions alone record the double answers.

OP-01/O66 (AX-6): D92 puts argument checks first in every state, Closed included, and D93 limits re-raising on a Failed stream to the data reads. D15, D16, D18, D52 and D70 still say every read on Failed re-raises and every read on Closed raises ValueError, so chunks(0) on a Failed stream gets two answers. How do they read?

options.label: Read as D92/D93 (Recommended)
options.description: Amend D15, D16, D18, D52 and D70: a caller error is raised first and leaves the state as it was. A valid data read (D93's list) on a Failed stream raises the failure again; a valid call on a Closed stream raises ValueError. chunks(0) on Failed: ValueError. This is io's order (O51 checked it) and O51's first answer, 'Reads only'.

options.label: State first on Failed
options.description: A Failed stream raises the failure again whatever the arguments, with D80 and D92 narrowed to Open, Exhausted and Closed. A caller's bug stays hidden behind the storage failure, which D80 rejected, and it departs from io.

questions.question: OP-01/O67 (AX-6): D94 says a cancelled close() leaves the stream Closed with its resources 'released or abandoned'. D50's cell and D20 say 'releases', and no register row says when an abandoned resource is freed. Which holds?

options.label: Released locally (Recommended)
options.description: A cancelled close() still frees every local resource. It aborts the connection instead of returning it to the pool, so nothing waits for garbage collection. D94's 'or abandoned' is withdrawn. Anything the backend still holds on its side (an SFTP file handle until its session ends) joins NP5's out-of-band effects. Source: asyncio Transport.abort() closes at once without waiting.

options.label: Admit abandoning
options.description: D50's cell reads 'releases or abandons; Closed', and the register gains NP10: when an abandoned resource is freed, like NP4 for an unclosed stream. Weaker: a pool slot or socket may stay held after a cancelled async-with exit.

questions.question: OP-01/O68 (AX-15): S3 changes metadata by copying the object onto itself. botocore's model says copied objects get an MD5 ETag, and multipart uploads do not (read, not run). So a metadata change on a multipart-uploaded object may change its ETag while the content stays the same, and an ETag-pinned resume fails changed. S3 declares no such deviation today. What does S3 declare?

options.label: Declare, unconditioned (Recommended)
options.description: D43's Pinned resume deviation, 'a metadata-only change also fails a resume changed', names S3 too, unconditionally. When unsure, take the weaker side (D43's reason). A check on S3 then accepts either outcome. E16, E18 and D84's tier move by copy follow from it.

options.label: Conditioned on the object
options.description: Declared only for objects that were multipart-uploaded or SSE-KMS/C-encrypted. This is a condition on the object, not on the location as D82 allows, and a check would have to know how each object was written.

options.label: Pin by version ID
options.description: On a versioned bucket, resume with the open's version ID, which serves the open's content even after a metadata change or a replace. Elsewhere pin by ETag, with the deviation declared. This adds a pin token and needs the s3:GetObjectVersion permission.

options.label: Keep normal value
options.description: S3 declares nothing, relying on the model's 'The ETag reflects only changes to the contents'. If the copy does change the ETag (not run), S3 deviates undeclared, which AX-15 forbids.

questions.question: OP-01/O69 (AX-15): D105 says D43's Decided-by column names every deciding decision per row. Several rows miss some (D77, D84, D88 to D90, D48, D97), and D110 claims the Read-after-write row names D105, which it does not. What does the column list?

options.label: Complete by rule (Recommended)
options.description: Each row lists every decision that changes what its normal value or a deviation lets a caller observe, plus D43's own restatements. Termination: D12, D13, D14, D57, D97. Read-after-write: D23, D63, D64, D76, D82, D83, D87, D105. Pinned resume: D22, D39, D42, D47, D61, D62, D72, D77, D84, D86, D102, plus O68's decision. O3 in-place: D26, D48, D99. Overlapping mutation: D65, D81, D83. Dual key: D67, D88 to D91. D110's check is reworded to state this rule. Lists come from a Grep for each row's decisions.

options.label: Drop the column
options.description: D43's rows cite no decisions; readers follow each decision's Amends and Amended-by links. Nothing left to drift, but D47, D77 and D84 amend no D43 text, so the links would not find them.

options.label: As is
options.description: Leave the column and D110 unchanged. O69 blocks nothing.
